summary: Mapped the wbase.ovr overlay's state machine and the main-menu state (state 4). wbase handles three master-state values: 4 (main menu), 7 (post-gameplay cleanup → back to menu), and 0x18=24 (configuration submenu). Entry dispatch is at file offset 0x0e (NOT 0x0c — header is 14 bytes, two more than winit's). The dispatch differs structurally from winit: states 4 and 7 use a *0x4fce 'pending next state' cache that the entry dispatcher copies into *0x363a after the handler returns; state 0x18 manages its own *0x363a write. The main menu (state 4 / FUN_2b36) is a 9-slot menu using the same generic FUN_025c selection-loop widget that wmaze uses (FUN_1574 in wmaze). Each enabled option's selected index is looked up via a CS-relative jump table at runtime address 0x731f which is actually stored inline in the overlay file at file offset 0x2dbb (delta 0x4564). The 9 handler addresses, the slot-enable rules, and the per-slot state transition are all extracted. Asset usage: FUN_064e(8, 4) loads font-table entry 4 with asset kind 8 — this is the MON08.PIC-equivalent decoration (gates + figure art). The dragonsc.scr top-stripe is NOT redrawn by wbase — it's persistent from winit state-2's draw and survives because wbase doesn't clear that region. Named 16 wbase.ovr functions including all 9 main-menu option handlers.
method: PyGhidra + capstone. Decoded the 14-byte overlay header (vs. winit's 12-byte header) and the 3-way state dispatch at file offset 0x0e by raw disasm. Then identified state-4 (main menu) at 0x2b36 by tracing the dispatch CALL targets. The menu loop was readable in decompiled C but its dispatch terminator JMP cs:[bx+0x731f] referenced an address beyond the file. Discovered the jump table is INLINE in the file at 0x2dbb, with the runtime BSS offset 0x731f mapping to file offset via a constant delta of 0x4564 (consistent runtime-image vs. file mapping for this overlay's data segment). Verified by disassembling at each computed handler address — every one is a coherent option-handler with a clear state transition. State-transition behavior was confirmed by exhaustively scanning the file for writes to *0x363a (game_state) and *0x4fce (next-state cache).

overlay_layout.header_difference_from_winit: wbase.ovr has a 14-byte overlay header (vs. winit's 12-byte). The bytes 0x0c..0x0d ('9f 7e') do not disassemble as code — they appear to be an extension to the relocation header. Real entry-dispatch code starts at file offset 0x0e.

data_segment_runtime_delta.claim: Runtime BSS/data offsets in cs:[disp16] addressing refer to data that's stored inline in the overlay file at (runtime_addr - 0x4564). Verified for the main-menu jump table at runtime 0x731f / file 0x2dbb. Same pattern likely applies to the state-7 sub-dispatch at runtime 0x7667 / file ~0x3103 and state-0x18 sub-dispatch at runtime 0x7cd1 / file ~0x376d, though not exhaustively verified.

state_var.scope: shared DGROUP (set by wroot's ovl_install_table at wroot 0x132d and read by all overlays)

next_state_cache.claim: Per-call cache used by wbase's entry dispatcher. After state-4 or state-7 handler returns, the dispatcher copies *0x4fce into *0x363a (effectively a deferred state transition). State 0x18 manages its own *0x363a write and the dispatcher skips the copy. State-4 itself does NOT write to *0x363a directly inside handlers EXCEPT to break the loop — instead handlers either set *0x4fce for a deferred transition or *0x363a directly to a non-negative value to exit the loop (and rely on the dispatcher's *0x4fce copy AT a later point). This is structurally different from winit (where handlers write *0x363a directly).

states_handled_in_wbase.name: STATE_MAIN_MENU
states_handled_in_wbase.purpose: Display the MASTER OPTIONS menu and dispatch to the chosen sub-action.
exit_transitions: Slot 1 (CHOOSE LEADER / start delve) → *0x363a := 0x11 (WPCVW), *0x4fce := 4 (return to menu after)
Slot 4 (RESUME SAVED GAME) → FUN_1a0d(1) which may set *0x363a := 6 (load zone) or 3 (quit fallback)
Slot 6 (GAME CONFIGURATION) → *0x4fce := 4, calls FUN_3151 (state-0x18 handler) directly
Slot 7 (SHOW TITLE PAGE) → *0x363a := 1 (back to winit title)
Slot 8 (QUIT GAME) → *0x363a := 3 (which ovl_install_table maps to abort_cleanup_dispatch + crt_run_atexit_and_exit)

states_handled_in_wbase.name: STATE_POST_GAMEPLAY_CLEANUP
states_handled_in_wbase.purpose: Free maze-data buffers (*0x4fa8, *0x4faa), destroy the dungeon-window (*0x4fb0), clear status/message windows, reset party_size := 0, transition back to state 4 (main menu).

states_handled_in_wbase.name: STATE_CONFIG_SUBMENU
states_handled_in_wbase.purpose: Configuration / options submenu. Loaded by ovl_install_table via FUN_36dc(0x5fa)=wbase (after boot_select_disk_for_content(1,0)). Also reachable in-process from main menu slot 6 (GAME CONFIGURATION) which sets *0x4fce := 4 and calls FUN_3151 directly. Renders text via msg ID 0x3e8, opens a 22x18 window at (19,40), draws a list of options. Inner dispatch uses a similar jump table at runtime 0x7667 / file ~0x3103.
states_handled_in_wbase.exit_transition: writes to *0x4fce (caches return-to-state); since dispatcher's *0x4fce → *0x363a copy is SKIPPED for state 0x18, the inner handler manages *0x363a directly. The slot-6 call path pre-sets *0x4fce := 4 so the configuration submenu's return path can come back to the main menu.

prologue_actions: func_c1f7(0x3e8, 0x5066) — load msg #1000 into the filename-style buffer at DGROUP 0x5066 (preparation for some load)

FUN_064e(8, 4) — load font/asset entry 4 of kind 8. Kind 8 is the same 'font table' kind that winit uses for WFONT/MAZEDATA, but this index loads the MON08-style menu decoration (castle gates + red figure art).
Clear/refresh windows *0x4fba and *0x4fb8 via func_ebb4 (a ui_window_clear variant)
For each existing party member i in 0..party_size-1: call FUN_1b2d(i) — draws party-panel for slot i

Call FUN_0984 — initializes background/menu decoration drawing (calls video-driver thunk 0xf148 with PIC descriptor IDs 0x15a, 0x15d, 0x160, ... and then FUN_07b7 which renders descriptors 0x7b, 0x7c, 0x7d, ...)
Set uStack_c (initial selection cursor offset) := 3 if party_size < 6, else 0

main_loop.loop_exit_condition: *0x363a >= 0  (handler set non-negative state to break out)
per_iteration_steps: FUN_01d6(0x3e9) — render banner 'MASTER OPTIONS' from msg ID 0x3e9
Create a list-window via func_bbb6(0, 0x13, 0x28, 5, 0xf, 0xffff, 0, 0) — geometry (x=19, y=40, w=5, h=15)
Initialize 9-slot options array on the stack: all slots := 1 (enabled); slot[9] := 0xffff (terminator)
Compute initial cursor position = FUN_2af7(options, uStack_c) — counts enabled options up to index uStack_c

Call FUN_025c(window, 0x3ea, options, 2, 1, 0x13, 4, 5, init_cursor) — generic menu select widget. Returns the selected ORIGINAL option index (0..8) via internal aiStack_24[] mapping. (msg base 0x3ea — option N labelled by msg ID 0x3ea+N)
Destroy the list window via func_bd6e
Dispatch on selected option index via inline jump table at file 0x2dbb (runtime addr 0x731f, accessed as cs:[bx + 0x731f] with bx = option*2)

rules: if any byte at *0x4fd8+i==1 for i in 0..*0x4fd2 then slot[0] := 1 (scan finds unloaded scenario characters)

entry_function.post_dispatch: Each handler ends with `jmp 0x2dda` which is `jmp 0x2bc1` (loop top). The loop body re-checks *0x363a — if still < 0, iterates; otherwise exits to function epilogue (mov sp,bp; pop bp; ret).

menu_options.label_hypothesis: ADD PARTY MEMBER (load existing character from PCFILE.DBS)
behavior: call FUN_253a — character-picker UI: pick a character from PCFILE.DBS (FUN_2143 returns -1 or character index)

If picked: load character data via FUN_0036, mark *0x4fd8+char_idx := 2 (slot used), store char_idx at *0x43dc+party_size*2, generate portrait via FUN_0c2c, draw via FUN_0b0e, memcpy 432 bytes to party slot at *0x43e8+party_size*0x1b0, draw party-panel via FUN_1b2d, increment party_size at *0x43ce
If party_size==6 after add: set local var [bp-0xa] := 3 (probably 'menu needs full redraw / re-init cursor')

menu_options.label_hypothesis: CHARACTER VIEW (party-leader pick → enter party-view screen). Likely 'INSPECT' or 'CHOOSE LEADER' depending on context.
behavior: call FUN_26c7(0x4b2) — character-picker among CURRENT party members. The arg 0x4b2 = msg ID 1202 is the picker-title text (likely 'CHOOSE LEADER' or 'PICK CHARACTER'). Returns -1 (cancel) or party-slot index.
Store result at *0x43cc (last-picked party slot)
If picked != -1: *0x363a := 0x11 (WPCVW), *0x4fce := 4 (return to main menu when done)
menu_options.transition: → state 0x11 (WPCVW — view player character / character screen)

menu_options.label_hypothesis: CHARACTER MENU / EDIT CHARACTER (pick a party member, then sub-menu).
behavior: call FUN_26c7(0x4b3) — character-picker with msg ID 1203 (likely 'EDIT CHARACTER' or similar)
Store result at *0x43cc
If picked != -1: call FUN_25cc(picked_index) — runs the character-edit / character-menu submenu inline (does NOT transition states — handles its own UI loop)
menu_options.transition: continues main-menu loop (no state change). The character-menu submenu finishes and returns here.

menu_options.label_hypothesis: REMOVE/UNLOAD ALL PARTY MEMBERS (resets party then probably opens load-game). Conditional on party_size >= 2.
behavior: Loop i = 0..party_size-1: set *0x4fd8+char_idx := 1 (mark available again) for each party member char_idx = *(0x43dc+i*2)
call FUN_1a0d(0) — game-load submenu with mode 0 (likely 'new game' or 'load-with-prompt')
menu_options.transition: FUN_1a0d sets *0x363a := 3 (quit) or := 6 (load zone) depending on success. Likely 'LEAVE GAME' or 'NEW GAME' depending on UX.

menu_options.label_hypothesis: RESUME SAVED GAME (only enabled when no current party).
behavior: call FUN_1a0d(1) — game-load submenu with mode 1 ('resume saved game')
menu_options.transition: FUN_1a0d sets *0x363a := 3 (failed/quit) or := 6 (loaded — enter game zone). On success, falls through to wmaze (state 5/6).

menu_options.label_hypothesis: MAKE CHARACTER / CREATE CHARACTER (state 0x10 = WPCMK overlay).
behavior: call FUN_2a70 — unload all party members (reverse loop calling FUN_25cc on each)
*0x363a := 0x10 (transition to WPCMK)

menu_options.label_hypothesis: GAME CONFIGURATION (in-process call to wbase's state-0x18 sub-handler).
behavior: *0x4fce := 4 (cache return-to-state)
call FUN_3151 — directly invokes the state-0x18 handler (configuration submenu) in-process
menu_options.transition: Stays in wbase. After FUN_3151 returns, the entry-dispatcher would normally copy *0x4fce → *0x363a, but the slot-6 handler is called from within state-4's loop, so this becomes part of the loop iteration. After FUN_3151 returns and the menu loop iterates, *0x363a is checked — if FUN_3151 set it to a non-negative value (transitioning), the loop exits.

menu_options.label_hypothesis: SHOW TITLE PAGE (back to winit title screen).
behavior: call FUN_2a70 — unload all party members
call FUN_2a83 — additional cleanup helper
*0x363a := 1 (transition to winit state 1: title page + credits)
call FUN_2a70 — unload all party members
call FUN_2a83 — additional cleanup helper
*0x363a := 3 (transition to quit)
menu_options.transition: → state 3 (QUIT — wroot's ovl_install_table case 3 calls abort_cleanup_dispatch(0) then crt_run_atexit_and_exit(0))

first_launch_visible_options.claim: On first launch with party_size==0, the enabled slots are: [0 (if PCFILE.DBS has any unloaded chars), 4, 5, 6, 7, 8] = 6 options visible. This matches the user-supplied screenshot of 6 menu items.
expected_labels_in_order: CHARACTER MENU       (slot 5, msg 0x3ef) — actually MAKE CHARACTER per state 0x10 = WPCMK
first_launch_visible_options.needs: Verify against actual msg.dbs decoded text — the msg IDs 0x3ea..0x3f2 (1002..1010) are outside the 718-entry indexedMessages range we extracted, so the encoding from a 'msg ID' to a msg.hdr index isn't a direct lookup. wmaze findings indicate func_c1f7 (load_msg_into_buf) does the ID-to-text resolution at wroot 0x75b; dynamic capture or a closer read of FUN_c1f7 would confirm the strings.

input_handling.input_function: FUN_013b at wbase file 0x13b — generic 'wait for menu input' (called from inside FUN_025c).
behavior: Sets *0x4fc4 := 0 (mouse-click flag reset)
Loop: kbd_check_with_filter(1). If no key:
call func_c674(param_2) — mouse-poll variant
If *0x3596 == 1 (mouse click captured): *0x4fc4 := 1, return (mouse_index - 1)
Run animation: alternate *0x3646 (frame parity), call FUN_07b7 to render frame, refresh window via func_f13c
Every 10 ticks, busy-wait via two delay calls
If key pressed: kbd_getkey_with_filter(1), call func_edec(param_1, key) for keypad/binding lookup
Returns the menu-navigation code: 1=up, 2=left, 3=down, 4=right, 5=ENTER (select), or click-driven index

loaded_in_state_4_prelude.asset: msg ID 0x3e8 (1000) — probably a filename or window-title string built into the DGROUP buffer at 0x5066

Font/PIC table entry 4 of kind 8. Kind 8 is the asset-table kind used by winit for WFONT/MAZEDATA loads (via wroot's c31e thunk → file table lookup). Index 4 in wbase's font-table area likely resolves to MON08.PIC — the gates+figure decoration art.
loaded_in_state_4_prelude.evidence: Pre-extracted MON08.PIC has descriptors matching the user's screenshot: desc 0 = arched stone gate, desc 1 = stone gate with figure, desc 2-5 = red figure / textured panels, desc 6 = banner-like text.
loaded_in_state_4_prelude.needs: Direct DOSBox-X trace of which file is opened during state-4 prelude to confirm MON08.PIC vs. other index.

loaded_in_state_4_prelude.asset: Per-descriptor sprite render calls. The thunk 0xf148 is in wroot's video-driver dispatch range (0xf100..0xf14x). The args 0x15a, 0x15d, 0x160 etc. are SPRITE/DESCRIPTOR IDs that the driver maps to (atlas, descriptor) tuples. FUN_07b7 then runs descriptors 0x7b, 0x7c, 0x7d, ... — these are likely the gates + figure descriptors from the loaded mon08.

background_dragonsc_stripe.claim: The 224-pixel-wide 'dragonsc' EGA top stripe with Wizardry letters + decorative icons (visible in the user's screenshot) is NOT loaded or drawn by wbase state-4. It is left over from winit state 2's font-table loading (which loaded TITLEPAG.{EGA|CGA|T16|HRC}) and persists because wbase's main menu doesn't clear the entire screen — it only clears specific window regions (0x4fba, 0x4fb8) and draws the menu over them. The top stripe is in a screen region that's never cleared between winit-state-2 and wbase-state-4.
background_dragonsc_stripe.needs: Direct screen-region trace in DOSBox-X to confirm which pixels are repainted when transitioning state 2 → state 4.

dgroup_state_variables.purpose: master state machine (shared with wroot, winit, wmaze)

dgroup_state_variables.purpose: wbase-only: deferred next-state value. After state-4 or state-7 handler returns, the entry dispatcher copies *0x4fce → *0x363a (transitioning to a new overlay). State 0x18 bypasses this copy.

dgroup_state_variables.name: party_size
dgroup_state_variables.purpose: Number of party members (0..6). Drives most menu-option enable rules.

dgroup_state_variables.purpose: Maps party slot index (0..5) to PCFILE.DBS character index. Read by slot-3 handler to unload chars, written by slot-0 (add) handler.

dgroup_state_variables.name: party_member_data_array
dgroup_state_variables.purpose: Full character data per party slot (432 bytes each). Written by FUN_253a's memcpy at slot-0 add.

dgroup_state_variables.purpose: Per-party portrait IDs generated by FUN_0c2c at add-time.

dgroup_state_variables.purpose: Per-character availability flag. 0 = unavailable, 1 = available (not in party), 2 = used (in party). Slot-0 enables itself if any byte == 1 here. Slot-3 sets back to 1 for each party member.
